content: 1. Administer 25-50 mg of dimenhydrinate orally every 6-8 hours as needed, ensuring the total daily dose does not exceed 150 mg for individuals over 12 years old. For motion sickness, administer 50-100 mg orally, intravenously, or intramuscularly every 4-6 hours as needed, ideally 30 minutes before exposure to motion, with a maximum daily dose of 400 mg. For maintenance, administer 25-50 mg orally every 8 hours, and for acute attacks, administer 50 mg intramuscularly. 2. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with calcium/magnesium/potassium/sodium oxybates can result in pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Avoid or use alternative drugs unless no other treatment options are adequate. Limit dosages and durations to the minimum required and monitor closely for signs of respiratory depression and sedation. 3. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with eluxadoline increases the risk of constipation-related serious adverse reactions due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and avoid combining with other drugs that cause constipation. 4. Dimenhydrinate and metoclopramide intranasal increase each other's effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs depending on the importance of the interacting drug to the patient. 5. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate and olopatadine intranasal increases the risk of central nervous system (CNS) depression, leading to additive psychomotor impairment and daytime sedation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Dimenhydrinate reduces the efficacy of pitolisant by antagonizing its pharmacodynamic effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as pitolisant increases histamine levels in the brain, and H1 receptor antagonists crossing the blood-brain barrier may counteract its effects. 7. Dimenhydrinate reduces the effects of secretin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Anticholinergic drugs may cause hyporesponsiveness to secretin stimulation testing. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 8. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with sodium oxybate can result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs unless no other treatment options are adequate. Limit dosages and durations to the minimum required and monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 9. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with zuranolone increases CNS depressant effects, potentially impairing psychomotor performance. If unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 10. Dimenhydrinate enhances the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for excessive neuromuscular weakness and systemic anticholinergic effects. 11. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with other sedative agents, such as acrivastine, albuterol, alfentanil, alprazolam, amisulpride, amitriptyline, amobarbital, amoxapine, amphetamine, apomorphine, arformoterol, aripiprazole, armodafinil, asenapine, azelastine, baclofen, belladonna and opium, benperidol, benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen, benzphetamine, benztropine, brexanolone, brexpiprazole, brimonidine, brivaracetam, brompheniramine, buprenorphine (various formulations), butabarbital, butalbital, butorphanol, caffeine, carbinoxamine, cariprazine, carisoprodol, chloral hydrate, chlordiazepoxide, chlorpheniramine, chlorpromazine, chlorzoxazone, cinnarizine, clemastine, clobazam, clomipramine, clonazepam, clonidine, clorazepate, clozapine, codeine, cyclizine, cyclobenzaprine, cyproheptadine, dantrolene, daridorexant, daxibotulinumtoxinA, desflurane, desipramine, desloratadine, deutetrabenazine, dexchlorpheniramine, dexfenfluramine, dexmedetomidine, dexmethylphenidate, dextroamphetamine, dextromoramide, diamorphine, diazepam (various formulations), diethylpropion, difelikefalin, diphenhydramine, diphenoxylate HCl, dipipanone, dobutamine, donepezil transdermal, dopamine, dopexamine, dosulepin, doxepin, doxylamine, droperidol, ephedrine, epinephrine (racemic), esketamine intranasal, estazolam, eszopiclone, ethanol, etomidate, fenfluramine, fentanyl (various formulations), flibanserin, fluphenazine, flurazepam, formoterol, gabapentin, gabapentin enacarbil, ganaxolone, and glycopyrrolate, increases the risk of sedation or CNS depression. Use caution, monitor closely, and modify therapy as needed. 12. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with gabapentin or gabapentin enacarbil can result in serious, life-threatening, or fatal respiratory depression. Use the lowest possible dose and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 13. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with flibanserin increases the risk of sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely, especially when flibanserin is combined with other CNS depressants. 14. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with fentanyl (various formulations) increases the risk of toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 15. Co-administration of dimenhydrinate with esketamine intranasal increases the risk of toxicity due to sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
